title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: fastDiversity provides fast flexible calculation standard population genetic diversity statistics biallelic SNP data. designed datasets samples span multiple populations, sites, species need analysed simultaneously, common scenario conservation genomics comparative population studies. package accepts genotype data standard biallelic dosage format: 0 (homozygous reference, aa), 1 (heterozygous, aA), 2 (homozygous alternate, AA), missing data NA. format output produced SNP-calling pipelines.

code: remotes::install_github("eilishmcmaster/fastDiversity") library(fastDiversity) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(ggthemes)

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: distance-based PCA provides intuitive overview genetic structure across individuals. PC scores computed pairwise genetic distances merged metadata plotting:  Clustering samples PCA space corroborates population structure indicated diversity statistics private allele analysis.
code: pca   <- prcomp(dist(example_gt), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE) s_pca <- summary(pca)  # Axis labels showing % variance explained importance <- s_pca[["importance"]][2, ] axis_names  <- paste0(names(importance), " (", round(importance * 100, 1), "%)")  # Merge PC scores with sample metadata pcs <- pca$x %>%   data.frame() %>%   merge(example_meta, by.x = 0, by.y = "sample")  ggplot(pcs, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = factor(population))) +   geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +   labs(     title  = expression("PCA of SNP genotypes"),     x      = axis_names[1],     y      = axis_names[2],     color  = "Population"   ) +   theme_bw()

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: Understanding alleles unique single population (private) versus shared across populations useful first step assessing population distinctiveness. Populations many private alleles may represent distinct evolutionary lineages warrant separate management.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: make_allele_list() takes genotype matrix grouping vector returns named list allele sets, one per group.
code: allele_list_population <- make_allele_list(example_gt, example_meta$population) #> There are 57 samples in 5 #> There are 31 samples in 4 #> There are 46 samples in 3 #> There are 23 samples in 2 #> There are 100 samples in 1  names(allele_list_population) #> [1] "5" "4" "3" "2" "1"

text: result standard named list, works directly ggvenn:  Alternatively, upset plot may easier read:  shows much allelic diversity shared across populations versus restricted individual groups. large exclusive region indicates genetically distinct population.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: faststats() calculates allelic richness, heterozygosity, inbreeding coefficients, population differentiation combination genetic group site, locus-level filtering applied independently within genetic group.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: Filtering applied within genetic group independently. locus retained one population may excluded another fails MAF missingness thresholds group, important distinction global pre-filtering, can retain uninformative loci groups discard informative ones others.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: genetic_group_variable defines level locus filtering applied (e.g. species population). site_variable defines grouping unit statistics calculated (e.g. sampling site). function returns one row per unique genetic group × site combination.
code: basicstats <- faststats(   gt                    = example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable         = example_meta$site,   minimum_n             = 6,   minimum_loci          = 50,   maf                   = 0.05,   max_missingness       = 0.3 ) #> 1 complete #> 2 complete #> 3 complete #> 4 complete #> 5 complete #> Process complete!  head(basicstats) #> # A tibble: 6 × 12 #>   group site      Ar    Ho    He   uHe     Fis    Gst    Fst    uFis  loci     n #>   <chr> <chr>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 1     Airdr…  1.68 0.268 0.256 0.283 -0.046  0.142  0.046   0.0527   844     6 #> 2 1     Big_S…  1.70 0.290 0.262 0.289 -0.104  0.122  0.0407 -0.0013   844     6 #> 3 1     Big_S…  1.72 0.262 0.269 0.297  0.0237 0.0999 0.0134  0.117    844     6 #> 4 1     Binna…  1.69 0.264 0.253 0.278 -0.0433 0.154  0.0604  0.0526   844     6 #> 5 1     Gibbe…  1.74 0.256 0.284 0.299  0.0997 0.0502 0.0153  0.145    844    11 #> 6 1     Koony…  1.59 0.233 0.220 0.244 -0.0626 0.265  0.166   0.0441   844     6

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: faststats() returns one row per site, population contributes multiple points, one per site. faceted multi-panel plot gives simultaneous overview heterozygosity, inbreeding, differentiation:
code: library(tidyr)  stats_long <- basicstats %>%   mutate(across(c(Ho, He, Fis, Fst), as.numeric)) %>%   pivot_longer(     cols      = c(Ho, He, Fis, Fst),     names_to  = "statistic",     values_to = "value"   ) %>%   mutate(statistic = factor(statistic,     levels = c("Ho", "He", "Fis", "Fst"),     labels = c("Observed heterozygosity (Ho)",                "Expected heterozygosity (He)",                "Inbreeding coefficient (Fis)",                "Fixation index (Fst)")   ))  ggplot(stats_long, aes(x = group, y = value, fill = group)) +   geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA) +   geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(~ statistic, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +   labs(     title = "Diversity statistics",     x     = "Population",     y     = NULL   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(     legend.position  = "none",     strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),     strip.text       = element_text(size = 9)   )

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: published reporting, bootstrapped confidence intervals can added around Ho, , Fis. Two resampling strategies available: loci (get_CI_loci_resampling = TRUE): analogous hierfstat::boot.ppfis : loci resampled replacement quantify sensitive statistics choice markers. individuals (get_CI_individual_resampling = TRUE): analogous diveRsity::basicstats : individuals resampled replacement quantify sampling uncertainty. CI columns appended prefix resampling strategy (loci_ ind_) suffix statistic quantile boundary (e.g. loci_ho.2.5%, loci_ho.97.5%). plug directly geom_pointrange():
code: basicstats_ci <- faststats(   gt                     = example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$site,   minimum_n              = 6,   minimum_loci           = 50,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3,   get_CI_loci_resampling = TRUE,   boots                  = 100,   CI_alpha               = 0.05 ) ggplot(basicstats_ci, aes(x = group, y = as.numeric(Ho), colour = group)) +   geom_pointrange(     aes(       ymin = as.numeric(`loci_ho.2.5%`),       ymax = as.numeric(`loci_ho.97.5%`)     ),     position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, seed = 1),     size = 0.6   ) +   labs(     title = expression("Ho ± 95% CI (loci bootstrap)"),     x = "Population",     y = "Observed heterozygosity (Ho)"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: faststats() can test whether allele frequencies site deviate significantly Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium expectations using Fisher’s exact test, p-values combined across loci using Fisher’s method: HW_fisher_p column gives combined p-value per site. Sites values chosen alpha threshold show significant deviation HWE, may reflect inbreeding, cryptic population structure within site, selection linked loci, genotyping artefacts.
code: basicstats_hwe <- suppressWarnings( faststats(   gt                     = example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   minimum_n              = 6,   minimum_loci           = 50,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3,   run_HWE_test           = TRUE,   return_locus_stats     = FALSE   # set TRUE to retrieve per-locus p-values ))  basicstats_hwe[,c("site", "Ho", "He", "Fis", "Fst", "loci", "n", "HWE_p")]

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: addition site-level summaries, fastDiversity provides two functions calculating statistics level individual samples. useful examining variation inbreeding heterozygosity individual basis, can informative fitness hybridisation. functions apply locus-level filtering faststats(): MAF missingness thresholds applied per genetic group calculation, ensuring individual estimates based high-quality, informative loci used population-level analyses.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: individual_Ho() calculates multilocus heterozygosity (MLH) sample: proportion retained loci heterozygous individual.
code: ind_MLH_ho <- individual_Ho(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3 )  head(ind_MLH_ho) #> NSW1008199 NSW1008169 NSW1008189 NSW1008229 NSW1008224 NSW1009574  #>  0.3719705  0.2673913  0.2556880  0.2719298  0.2706522  0.3679834

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: individual_F() calculates Wright’s inbreeding coefficient sample: F = 1 − (Ho / ), calculated across genetic group. measures probability alleles locus identical descent (Frankham, Ballou & Briscoe 2010). calculated group level rather across genetic groups, estimates deflated Wahlund effect arise pooling genetically differentiated individuals.
code: ind_F <- individual_F(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3 )  head(ind_F) #> NSW1008199 NSW1008169 NSW1008189 NSW1008229 NSW1008224 NSW1009574  #> 0.01264873 0.29024170 0.32130680 0.27819474 0.28158612 0.02323208

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: Plotting individual MLH F reveals expected negative relationship: individuals higher observed heterozygosity lower inbreeding coefficients.
code: # Combine into a data frame and add population labels ind_df <- data.frame(   sample     = names(ind_MLH_ho),   MLH        = as.numeric(ind_MLH_ho),   F          = as.numeric(ind_F) ) %>%   merge(example_meta, by = "sample")  ggplot(ind_df, aes(x = MLH, y = F, colour = as.factor(population))) +   geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +   labs(     title    = expression("Individual MLH vs inbreeding coefficient"),     x        = "Multilocus heterozygosity (Ho)",     y        = expression(paste("Inbreeding coefficient (", italic(F), ")")),     colour   = "Population"   ) +   theme_bw()

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: pi_theta_d_stats() calculates nucleotide diversity (pi), Wu & Watterson’s theta (W), number segregating sites (S), Tajima’s D genetic site_variable specified within genetic_group_variable. implementation follows missing-data-aware approach Korunes & Samuk (2021), meaning loci missing genotypes contribute proportionally rather excluded entirely, important correction RADseq DArTseq data missingness common.

title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: n = NULL, individuals site used. n argument can set fixed integer subsample individuals, allows comparison across sites unequal sample sizes:
code: # Use all available individuals per population D_n_all <- pi_theta_d_stats(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   n                      = NULL,   minimum_n              = 5,   minimum_loci           = 5,   max_missingness        = 0.1,   maf                    = 0,   allele_count_min       = 0 ) #> Process complete!  # Subsample to 20 individuals per population D_n_20 <- pi_theta_d_stats(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   n                      = 20,   minimum_n              = 5,   minimum_loci           = 5,   max_missingness        = 0.1,   maf                    = 0,   allele_count_min       = 0 ) #> Process complete!  # Subsample to 10 individuals per population D_n_10 <- pi_theta_d_stats(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   n                      = 10,   minimum_n              = 5,   minimum_loci           = 5,   max_missingness        = 0.1,   maf                    = 0,   allele_count_min       = 0 ) #> Process complete!  # Subsample to 5 individuals per population D_n_5 <- pi_theta_d_stats(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   n                      = 5,   minimum_n              = 5,   minimum_loci           = 5,   max_missingness        = 0.1,   maf                    = 0,   allele_count_min       = 0 ) #> Process complete!

what: Effect of sample size on diversity estimates
title: Introduction to fastDiversity
text: key feature pi_theta_d_stats() n argument, subsamples individuals fixed number calculation. allows fair comparison across populations unequal sample sizes. However, sample size affects estimates differently: S particularly sensitive n larger samples likely capture rare variants, inflates W relative pi therefore pulls D negative. plot illustrates comparing estimates across three levels subsampling:
code: library(tidyr)  # Combine results and label by sample size used D_combined <- bind_rows(   D_n_all %>% mutate(sample_size = paste0("All (n=", n, ")")),   D_n_20  %>% mutate(sample_size = "n = 20"),   D_n_10  %>% mutate(sample_size = "n = 10"),   D_n_5   %>% mutate(sample_size = "n = 5") ) %>%   mutate(     across(c(pi, S, theta, D), as.numeric),     sample_size = factor(sample_size,                          levels = c("n = 5", "n = 10", "n = 20",                                     unique(D_n_all %>%                                              mutate(l = paste0("All (n=", n, ")")) %>%                                              pull(l))))   )  # Reshape to long for faceting D_long <- D_combined %>%   pivot_longer(cols = c(pi, S, theta, D),                names_to  = "statistic",                values_to = "value") %>%   mutate(statistic = factor(statistic,     levels = c("pi", "theta", "S", "D"),     labels = c("Nucleotide diversity (pi)",                "Wu & Watterson's theta (W)",                "Segregating sites (S)",                "Tajima's D")))  ggplot(D_long, aes(x = group, y = value, colour = sample_size,                    group = sample_size)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   facet_wrap(~ statistic, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +   labs(     title   = expression("Effect of sample size on diversity statistics"),     x       = "Population",     y       = NULL,     colour  = "Sample size"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(     strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),     strip.text       = element_text(size = 9),     legend.position  = "bottom"   )

what: Simple and Quick Diversity Calculations for Biallelic Data
title: Simple and Quick Diversity Calculations for Biallelic Data
text: Documentation: https://eilishmcmaster.github.io/fastDiversity/ fastDiversity R package fast, flexible calculation population genetic diversity statistics biallelic SNP data. Many existing tools require specific file formats data structures, longer actively maintained. fastDiversity designed work directly SNP dataset encoded standard biallelic dosage format (0 (homozygous reference, aa), 1 (heterozygous, aA), 2 (homozygous alternate, AA), NA missing data), direct output SNP-calling pipelines. key design goal support datasets spanning multiple species genetic groups, locus filtering statistics need calculated independently per group. common scenario conservation genomics comparative population studies well served existing tools.

title: Simple and Quick Diversity Calculations for Biallelic Data
text: tutorial vignette available online https://eilishmcmaster.github.io/fastDiversity/articles/fastDiversity-intro.html. build vignette locally, install additional dependencies first:
code: # Install remotes if needed if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")  remotes::install_github("eilishmcmaster/fastDiversity")  library(fastDiversity) install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown", "ggplot2", "ggthemes", "tidyr",                    "ggvenn", "ggVennDiagram")) remotes::install_github("eilishmcmaster/fastDiversity", build_vignettes = TRUE) browseVignettes("fastDiversity")

title: Simple and Quick Diversity Calculations for Biallelic Data
text: Allele sharing private alleles: Diversity statistics: Returns one row per genetic group × site combination, columns Ho, , uHe, Fis, uFis, Gst (Nei 1973), population-specific Fst (Weir & Goudet 2017), rarefied allelic richness (Ar), number individuals loci used. bootstrapped confidence intervals: Individual-level statistics: functions apply MAF missingness filtering per genetic group calculation, individual estimates based loci used population-level analyses. Neutrality statistics: Returns table containing nucleotide diversity (pi), segregating sites (S), Wu & Watterson’s theta (W), Tajima’s D (D) per site_variable grouping. full worked example plots, see tutorial vignette.
code: library(fastDiversity)  data(example_data)  # loads two objects:                     #   example_gt:   genotype matrix, samples × loci, values 0/1/2/NA                     #   example_meta: sample metadata with population and site columns allele_list <- make_allele_list(example_gt, example_meta$population)  # Visualise overlap between populations ggvenn::ggvenn(allele_list)  # Count private and total alleles per population calculate_private_alleles(allele_list) basicstats <- faststats(   gt                     = example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$site,   minimum_n              = 3,   minimum_loci           = 50,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3 ) basicstats_ci <- faststats(   gt                     = example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$site,   minimum_n              = 3,   minimum_loci           = 50,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3,   get_CI_loci_resampling = TRUE,   # resample loci   boots                  = 100,   CI_alpha               = 0.05 ) # Individual multilocus heterozygosity (MLH) ind_MLH_ho <- individual_Ho(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3 )  # Individual inbreeding coefficient (Wright's F = 1 - Ho/He) # He is calculated at the genetic group level, avoiding Wahlund effect inflation ind_F <- individual_F(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   maf                    = 0.05,   max_missingness        = 0.3 )  plot(ind_MLH_ho, ind_F) # Use all available individuals per population D_n_all <- pi_theta_d_stats(   example_gt,   genetic_group_variable = example_meta$population,   site_variable          = example_meta$population,   n                      = NULL, # if set to NULL, all individuals are used, but downsampling can be specified   minimum_n              = 5,    minimum_loci           = 5,   max_missingness        = 0.1,   maf                    = 0,   allele_count_min       = 0 )

title: Calculate basic diversity statistics — faststats
code: faststats(   gt,   genetic_group_variable,   site_variable,   minimum_n = 3,   minimum_loci = 50,   maf = 0.05,   max_missingness = 0.3,   get_CI_loci_resampling = FALSE,   loci_resample_n = NULL,   get_CI_individual_resampling = FALSE,   individual_resample_n = NULL,   boots = 100,   CI_alpha = 0.05,   run_HWE_test = FALSE,   return_locus_stats = FALSE )

title: Calculate basic diversity statistics — faststats
text: gt Genotype matrix individuals rows loci columns, coded 0=aa, 1=aA, 2=AA. genetic_group_variable Vector genetic group IDs individual (length number rows gt). Can represent species, subspecies, biologically relevant structure groups. site_variable Vector group IDs (sites) individual (length number rows gt). minimum_n Minimum number individuals required per site (sites fewer individuals filtered ). minimum_loci Minimum number loci required proceed analysis genetic group (genetic groups fewer loci skipped). maf Minimum minor allele frequency filter. max_missingness Maximum proportion missing data allowed per locus (loci higher missingness filtered ). get_CI_loci_resampling Get confidence intervals Ho, , Fis, using bootstrapping resampling loci (hierfstat::boot.ppfis) loci_resample_n Number loci resample bootstrapping, defaults site n. get_CI_individual_resampling Get confidence intervals Ho, , Fis, using bootstrapping resampling individuals (diveRsity::basicstats) individual_resample_n Number samples resample bootstrapping, defaults site n. boots Number bootstraps get confidence intervals. CI_alpha Alpha value confidence intervals, defaults 0.05 (2.5%, 97.5% CIs). run_HWE_test Specify whether statistically test allele frequencies differ Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. return_locus_stats Specify whether return p values locus HWE testing. Setting TRUE also runs HWE test (run_HWE_test = TRUE).

title: Calculate basic diversity statistics — faststats
text: data frame following columns (, return_locus_stats = TRUE,   list data frame summary per-locus HWE p-values locus_HWE): group Genetic group ID (e.g., species, subspecies). site Site ID corresponding sample location. Ar Rarefied allelic richness: expected number alleles per locus sample     smallest size observed locus among sites retained genetic group,     averaged across loci (see calculate_rarified_Ar). Comparable among sites within     genetic group. Ho Observed heterozygosity. Expected heterozygosity Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium within site_variable. uHe Unbiased expected heterozygosity (corrected small sample size). Fis Inbreeding coefficient (Fis = 1 - Ho / ). Gst Site-level gene diversity differentiation sense Nei (1973),     (Ht - Hs) / Ht, Hs site's Ht individuals     genetic group. Fst Population-specific Fst Weir & Goudet (2017) site, relative     sites retained genetic group (see calculate_Fst). NA group     one retained site. uFis Unbiased inbreeding coefficient (uFis = 1 - Ho / uHe). loci Number loci used analysis group-site combination. n Number individuals sampled site given group. *_ci.*%, *_ci.*% Lower upper confidence intervals Fis, Ho, , generated via bootstrapping. Column prefixes indicate statistic (e.g., loci_f.2.5%, loci_he.97.5%). HWE_p P-value Fisher's method combining Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium tests across loci (HardyWeinberg::HWExact).

title: fastDiversity (development version)
text: faststats(): previous Fst column, (Ht - Hs) / Ht, mislabelled Weir & Cockerham (1984). now named Gst (Nei 1973). new Fst column gives population-specific FST (Weir & Goudet 2017) site, relative retained sites genetic group. New calculate_Fst(): population-specific FST (Weir & Goudet 2017); matches hierfstat::fs.dosage(). faststats(): Ar now rarefied allelic richness, documented, using calculate_rarified_Ar() across retained sites genetic group. Previously mean number alleles per individual (1 + Ho). calculate_Ar(): now returns (unrarefied) mean number alleles observed per locus. Previously returned 1 + Ho. calculate_rarified_Ar(): uses log-scale binomial coefficients (previously overflowed 0 large samples), returns NA loci genotyped every site, returns site locus names, handles single-individual sites; matches hierfstat::allelic.richness() complete data.

title: fastDiversity (development version)
text: make_allele_list() / matcher(): alleles assigned using DArT 1-row coding (2 = heterozygote) instead package’s 0=aa, 1=aA, 2=AA coding. Private total allele counts calculate_private_alleles() change result, now agree calculate_total_alleles(). faststats(): statistic columns now numeric (previously character). faststats(): return_locus_stats = TRUE longer errors run_HWE_test = FALSE; now runs HWE test automatically. resampling_loci_CI(), resampling_individuals_CI(): longer call set.seed(14) internally, overwrote user’s random number state. Use set.seed() calling reproducible intervals. MC_HWEtest_of_loci(): matrix input now works (previously data frames), per-locus “genotypes labelled” warnings gone. individual_Ho(): longer errors group loci. faststats(): statistics calculated full precision rounded output (per-locus previously rounded averaging). faststats(): groups loci pass missingness filter skipped message instead erroring. faststats(): bootstrap CIs longer error resampled values NA. pi_theta_d_stats(): minimum_loci now applied (ignored), statistic columns numeric, sites single remaining locus segregating sites longer error.

title: fastDiversity (development version)
text: C++ helpers compiled package instead runtime Rcpp::cppFunction(), bootstrapping much faster compiler needed installation. Progress output uses message() instead print()/cat(), can silenced suppressMessages(). Unused future.apply dependency removed. Example dataset documented (?example_data). Expanded test suite checks hand-calculated values. pkgdown documentation site R CMD check GitHub Action added.

title: fastDiversity 1.3.0
text: calculate_pi_theta_d(): reimplemented vectorised approach improved performance. Non-segregating monomorphic sites now removed prior calculation. function now accepts gt matrix format used throughout package. Return value structure changed: function now returns tajima_d, num_sites, raw_pi, watterson_theta, d_stdev (previously returned pi, S, theta, D, per_site_stats).
